input.command:
cd /Users/tony_vi/.warp/worktrees/code-assistants/chamisa-badger
R=awinogradov/code-assistants
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tony-vi--warp-worktrees-code-assistants-chamisa-badger/a0f2285c-709e-4de2-9866-569a01e1e104/scratchpad
OLD=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
cat > "$SP/i503.txt" <<'EOF'
feat(plan): record passes and exit reason with the score

- Extend the recorded Score line with the passes spent and why the
  revision loop ended: target reached, no improvement, or budget spent
- Name the weakest dimension when the score fell short of the target
- Document the same line in the chapter 5 pipeline walkthrough
- Assert the exit reasons, the weakest clause, and both copies
EOF
bunx --no -- commitlint < "$SP/i503.txt" >/dev/null && echo "commitlint OK"
git reset --soft HEAD~1 && git add -A
git commit -F "$SP/i503.txt" --quiet 2>&1 | grep -vE '^\[(STARTED|COMPLETED|SKIPPED)\]' | tail -1
echo "✓ $(git log -1 --format=%s)"
git diff --stat $OLD..HEAD
git push --force-with-lease origin issue-503-record-scoring-data 2>&1 | tail -1
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
cat > "$SP/r510.md" <<EOF
Fixed in [${SHA:0:7}](https://github.com/awinogradov/code-assistants/commit/$SHA).

Correct, and it was the half of the sample that matters most for the question #503 asks. Recording that a plan landed at 97 tells you the bar was missed; recording that Testability was the weakest dimension tells you *why*, which is what distinguishes "the threshold is too high" from "plans are consistently weak in one place". Dropping the clause would have left the below-target case recording a number with no indication of what was weak, and nothing would have failed.

The guard now asserts the \`weakest:\` token in the format line, the surrounding prose in both copies, and mutation-tested both directions: removing \`[ · weakest: <dimension>]\` from the format fails the score-line assertion, and removing the clause from chapter 5 fails the parity assertion.
EOF
body=$(python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.dumps({'body':open(sys.argv[1]).read()}))" "$SP/r510.md")
printf '%s' "$body" | gh api -X POST "repos/$R/pulls/510/comments/3681076298/replies" --input - --jq '"✓ replied -> \(.html_url)"'
